summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 43.4% YoY to INR426 crores, with same-store sales growth of 28.7% and pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin of 8.1%.
summary.overview: United Foodbrands (Barbeque Nation) reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR426 crores, up 43.4% YoY, with consolidated SSSG of 28.7% on top of 14.4% in Q4 FY26. Growth was volume-led (dine-in transactions up 63.5%) with no price increase taken. Pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.1% from about 5.5% in Q4 and roughly 350 bps higher YoY, helped by a 130 bps sequential gross margin recovery in Barbeque Nation India. International gross margin fell on Middle East-linked food inflation, and net debt rose marginally to INR106 crores.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation India
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth 33.5%, revenue growth 43.4%, dine-in transactions up 68.6%; gross margin up ~130 bps QoQ. Captive digital ecosystem drives 65% of dine-in transactions (from ~61% in Q4); MAUs ~1.4 million, up ~60% YoY.

segments.name: Barbeque Nation International
segments.commentary: Revenue growth 46.6%, SSSG 8.5%, dine-in volume growth 45.2%, gross profit up 40.3%. Restaurant operating margin 18.7%, but gross margin down ~3 pp on Middle East-linked inflation; added 1 UAE restaurant.

segments.name: Premium casual dining (Premium CDR)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth ~36%, SSSG 13.6%, dine-in volume growth ~40%. Mature restaurants deliver restaurant operating margin of upwards of 20%; added 1 and closed 1 restaurant, network unchanged. Q4 FY26 cohort expected to lift segment margin.

guidance_outlook: SSSG expected to moderate through FY27 as comparables tighten, with Q3 and Q4 FY27 lapping the strongest quarter of FY26; management called this a base effect, not weaker demand.

Margin levers for FY27: gross margin recovery in India, mature portfolio ROM expansion, new-store cohort maturation and back-end cost leverage; management did not give a pre-Ind AS double-digit EBITDA margin timeline.
Target of 300 restaurants by FY27 (about 40 additions this year vs ~35 last year); 15 restaurants under construction to operationalise in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex guided at ~INR140 crores (INR120 crores for new outlets, INR20 crores maintenance and ancillary), per the prior guidance reiterated on the call.
Management sees Barbeque Nation India capable of ~600 restaurants at current scale, up from an earlier view of 400-450, given the Big Buffet format in Tier 2/3 markets.
Momentum said to be continuing into July; revenue crossed INR400 crores for the first time, and the quarter ended at about INR425 crores.
capex_capacity: Restaurant count closed Q1 FY27 at 266 after 5 additions; target of 300 by FY27 maintained.
15 restaurants under construction, expected to open in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
Barbeque Nation India store format reduced to ~3,500 sq ft from 4,500 sq ft; newer format's revenue per restaurant said to be among the highest.
Expansion funded largely from internal accruals; borrowings to be kept at prudent levels.
demand_pricing: Growth described as entirely volume-led; no price increase taken in Q1 despite inflation. Average per-cover spend declined due to value initiatives from Q2 FY26 and has now stabilised at Q4 FY26 levels.
Average revenue per mature restaurant is around INR7 crores; management has not given a target for the next step.
Repeat business is ~45-47% of the base, with the new-vs-repeat mix shifting slightly toward new guests. Average bill is ~4.3 pax, and repeat tracking relies on one mobile number per bill.

Delivery growth of 62% was supported by value SKUs across Barbeque Nation, BBQ and Dum Safar brands and by higher marketing spend. Delivery share of mix rose ~2 pp YoY and carries commission and packaging costs of about 30%.
Management described the mature cost base as 'normalised' after recent hires in culinary, marketing and digital; each INR1 per-cover improvement adds about INR1.5 crores of annual cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: How much more market does Big Buffet open up in Tier 3/4 markets, versus two years ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Big Buffet has about 6 quarters of data in Tier 2/3 markets, with some sites as small as 3 lakh population. It sees Barbeque Nation India able to reach about 600 restaurants at current scale, versus an earlier view of 400-450.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the SSSG improvement, by brand?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-led volume strategy began in Barbeque Nation India, then extended to International and premium CDR. Marketing spend rose about 1 pp of revenue, and digital conversion investments were added. Average revenue per mature restaurant is about INR7 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is mature-portfolio ROM (16.2%) below the ~20% implied by flow-through math?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the ~400 bps shortfall to about 2 pp lower gross margin, about 1 pp higher marketing, about 60 bps from delivery mix (delivery costs about 30%), and about 140-150 bps of energy, manpower and other inflation. It said it would not cap margins at 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the back-end cost base still rising and what is the per-cover sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost base is now normalised after hires in culinary, marketing, digital and tech; the April increments were the only incremental impact. Each INR1 per-cover improvement adds about INR1.5 crores of annual cost.

qa_highlights.question: What drives delivery growth, and what is its profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Delivery grew 62% on value SKUs across Barbeque Nation, BBQ and Dum Safar, plus higher marketing. Management said delivery is non-captive, depends on aggregators, and is accretive only if it adds absolute margin; it did not disclose delivery profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q2 guidance levels of high single digit to early double digit SSSG still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a full-year SSSG number, pointing instead to volume growth and a new operating scale. It said the momentum continued into July and revenue crossed INR400 crores for the first time, with the quarter at about INR425 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international gross margin impact and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: International gross margin fell about 3 pp on Middle East-linked inflation, with some commodity prices up 30-40%. Management expects it to taper sequentially but said some structural reversal may not occur.

risks_watch: SSSG moderation through FY27: Q3 and Q4 FY27 lap the strongest FY26 quarters, and management guided that reported growth will normalise.
Gross margin pressure from mix (BBQ India growing faster than the lower-GM segments) and from Middle East-linked commodity inflation in International, with some commodity prices up 30-40%.
Service and food quality: April manpower disruption, some guest reviews on service and AC, and a recent food-blogger video on chicken quality, which management disputed without lab detail.
Delivery economics: about 30% commission and packaging costs, delivery share up about 2 pp YoY, and no disclosed delivery margin.
Store expansion execution: 40 openings planned for FY27 against 35 last year, with 15 under construction, and a new 3,500 sq ft format; watch whether 266 to 300 is met.
No double-digit pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin timeline given; watch the margin levers on gross margin, mature ROM and new-store cohort maturation.
key_quotes: Our growth continues to be entirely volume led. We have not taken any price increase during Q1, and our average per coverage spend continues to reflect changes in business segment mix, daypart and session mix and value-led initiatives that we started from Q2 FY26.
This is more mathematics than our comment on demand.
I think the current levels of around 66% -67% range is a good operating band and we would expect to move directionally from here over time.
And as long as the absolute EBITDA margins are better, I'm not too worried about gross margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume momentum and unit economics, with explicit caution on the margin trajectory, gross margin and inflation. Management was evasive on full-year SSSG and on a timeline to double-digit EBITDA margin, pointing to levers instead.
